name: astral-3d
description: The Thermo Astral analyser: an asymmetric-track multi-reflection time-of-flight instrument, modelled entirely from published information. Two elongated mirrors face each other across a 40 mm board gap; ions oscillate between them while drifting along their length, and the mirrors converge slightly so the drift decelerates and reverses. Each mirror is a two-dimensional cross-section whose extrusion axis is tilted by half the convergence, which makes the field anisotropy Ez/Ex exactly tan(alpha) instead of a quantity no affordable three-dimensional mesh can resolve - see docs/astral-handoff.md sections 12 and 13. The two solves carry one mirror at potential with the other grounded, which is the ordinary basis decomposition and therefore exact. The ion foil is not included: its shape is measured in section 11 and the drift force it produced was 5.7 times what the published reversal needs, so it is a study rather than part of the shipped device. The third element is the ion foil: a volume solve carrying the four shaped plates at their graded bias with every mirror strip grounded, which is the basis field psi_foil. The tilt supplies a0 = 0.84 of the drift pseudopotential and the stripe the remaining 0.16, which Grinfeld et al. give in closed form; an earlier revision of this template said the tilt was only 31 to 38 per cent of what was needed, and that was an artefact of a tilt baseline wrong by a factor of two. Measured here at a0 = 0.8504 against the published 0.83999.

ionEnergy.description: Nominal beam energy. Stewart et al.: 4 keV entering the analyser.

spacerThickness.description: Thickness of the spacer that tilts the mirrors relative to one another. PUBLISHED: Stewart et al. give 200 microns. What it is not published over is the baseline - see tiltBaseline - and that is the whole of the uncertainty in the drift reversal.

tiltBaseline.description: Length the spacer tilts each mirror over, so the tilt angle is asin(spacerThickness / tiltBaseline). PUBLISHED as of 2026-09-04: Grinfeld et al. give the convergence as 0.045 deg BETWEEN the mirrors, which over a 0.2 mm spacer is a 509.3 mm baseline. Two independent routes agree - requiring the tilt to supply the published a0 = 0.83999 of the drift pseudopotential wants 515.9 mm, 1.3% away. This was 250 mm and flagged as the most consequential guess in the reconstruction, carrying a 2.8-fold ambiguity; it was wrong by almost exactly a factor of two.

injectionAngle.description: Tangent of the angle between the trajectory and the mirror axis, setting the drift rate as V tan(theta). PUBLISHED as of 2026-09-04: Grinfeld et al. Table 1 gives a nominal 1.78 deg, and this is its tangent. Was 0.03998 (2.29 deg), inferred by requiring the reversal to land at 335 mm with the tilt baseline also wrong - the two errors compensated, which is why the geometric register reproduced anyway.

driftLength.description: Extent along the drift, and hence the extent of the foil. Published nominal drift is 335 mm, but this must be LONGER: where the stripe ends its contribution to the drift potential decays and partly cancels the tilt's continuing rise, leaving a crest an ion with slightly more sideways energy can clear. With the foil coextensive with a 350 mm drift that crest sat 2.3% above the nominal drift energy while the design's operating range is 2.2%, and the reversal jumped from 338.6 to 409.1 mm for a 1.1% change in injection angle. At 450 mm the crest moves to 435 mm and demands 6.3 V against the ion's 4.8. See docs/astral-handoff.md section 48.

capToCap.description: Cap plate to cap plate. Set so the EFFECTIVE mirror separation - the ion's nominal velocity times the half period, which is what Grinfeld et al. Table 1 states - comes out at the published 641 mm. Measured 641.1 mm at this value, and dL_eff/dcapToCap is 0.983, so the mirror dwell is essentially unchanged by the setting. The published 641 is an effective distance and NOT a physical cap-to-cap, so it cannot be used here directly.

boardGap.description: Board-to-board separation at the drift mid-point.

boardThickness.description: How thick each board is in y.

vacuumPad.description: Vacuum between the outermost metal and the solve boundary.

detectorInset.description: How far inside the far end the collecting plane sits.

d1.description: Depth at which U1 is reached, from the mirror mouth. FREE: no paper states the electrode lengths, and they are what the published coefficients were optimised against. Free parameter of the inverse problem: the published potential coefficients were optimised against Thermo geometry, so applying them to these depths gives a mirror that is not at its own focus. Fit against focusingC1, whose magnitude is 21.5 times the reciprocal energy spread here and should fall by orders when first order cancels.

d2.description: Depth at which U2 is reached, from the mirror mouth. STILL FREE - no paper states the electrode lengths - but no longer arbitrary: at 38 mm the sensitivity dc1/dTE1 comes out 0.987 against the 1.0 implied by the published C(1) vector, where the previous 50 mm gave 2.2. Measured at TE1 = 0, which is where the published statement applies.

d3.description: Depth at which U3 is reached, from the mirror mouth. STILL FREE. At 84 mm the mirror reaches the best resolving power found so far once TE1 and TE2 are solved to cancel the first and second order time-energy coefficients: R = 4,466 at a +/-3% energy spread, against 1,335 at 90 mm and 626 at 96 mm. What remains is c3 = 2.07, and cancelling that is a condition on these depths - see docs/astral-handoff.md section 49.

d4.description: Depth at which U4 is reached, from the mirror mouth. FREE: no paper states the electrode lengths, and they are what the published coefficients were optimised against. Free parameter of the inverse problem: the published potential coefficients were optimised against Thermo geometry, so applying them to these depths gives a mirror that is not at its own focus. Fit against focusingC1, whose magnitude is 21.5 times the reciprocal energy spread here and should fall by orders when first order cancels.

mouth.description: Distance from the cap plate to the mirror mouth, so the mirror occupies x from mouth - d4 to mouth and the field-free gap is what is left. INDEPENDENT of d4 as of 2026-09-02; it used to be defined as d4, which meant varying the electrode depths walked the two mirror mouths together and shrank the field-free gap - physically right for a fixed envelope, where depth and drift length are one degree of freedom rather than two, but it makes a scan over the depths a scan along a trade. Separating them is what makes fitting d1..d4 against the energy focus well posed. Handoff section 16.

detectorZ.description: kept for reference: where a detector at the FAR end of the drift would sit. The shipped detector is behind the launch point instead, because an asymmetric-track analyser's ions drift out, reverse, and come back - catching them at the far end measures only the outbound half and hides the behaviour the device is named for.

mirrorTilt.description: Tilt of each mirror, in half turns. The near stack takes +mirrorTilt and the far -mirrorTilt, which brings both mouths toward the mid-plane as z increases.

zPad.description: how far the solve domain and the electrode stripes run beyond the drift at each end. The reversal convergence moves 7.4% from 0 to 50 mm and 0.4% from 50 to 150, so this is converged; at zero the Neumann face sits 10 mm from where the ion turns round.

foilVolts.description: Foil bias, uniform across the contoured plate. PUBLISHED range 0 to -20 V. Shipped at -3 V as of 2026-09-02, which is where the drift becomes first-order isochronous on the full track: the return time's dependence on v_z0 falls from the bare tilt's (dT/T)/(dv/v) = +1.00 to +0.046, zero near -3.2 V, and the flight time lands at 800 us against a published ~779 (784.85 at -4 V). The reversal point does not move with the bias (335.6 mm against 334.6 without it) because the x-averaged well is nearly equal at injection and reversal, so the foil is a pure timing correction. At -20 V it overshoots to -0.93. What remains is second order, about -6.5, which is the well not being harmonic. Handoff section 22.

foilThickness.description: how thick the foil electrodes are.

foilGap.description: Half-gap between the foil plates in the board-gap direction. Defaults to halfGap, so the foil is a shaped conductive region on the inner face of each board rather than a separate aperture in the flight path - which is both the plausible construction for a printed-circuit analyser and what the published schematic projects to. Mounting the plates flush costs 15% of the well depth (7.31 V against 8.58 V at foilGap 8 mm) and leaves the well shape unchanged, shallowest at 41% of the drift and deepest at 67%.

foilSlices.description: Number of constant-width boxes the contoured foil plate is built from. The contour runs along the drift, so each slice spans a range of drift and holds one inner-edge position.

foilOuterFrac.description: Foil plate outer edge, as a fraction of the mid-plane to mirror-mouth distance. Measured from the published schematic at 146 mm of 182 mm; the outer edge is straight to within one pixel over the whole drift.

foilInnerMid.description: Mean position of the foil plate inner edge, as a fraction of the mid-plane to mirror-mouth distance. The inner edge is contoured along the drift; this is the midpoint of that contour.

foilInnerAmplitude.description: Half the peak-to-peak excursion of the foil inner edge along the drift. The published schematic gives 0.641 of the reach at the plate thinnest and 0.515 at its thickest.

foilThinAt.description: Drift fraction at which the foil plate is thinnest, so its inner edge lies furthest from the axis and the gap between the two plates is widest.

foilThickAt.description: Drift fraction at which the foil plate is thickest, so its inner edge lies closest to the axis and the gap between the two plates is narrowest. Half a contour wavelength past foilThinAt.

foilStartFrac.description: Drift fraction at which the foil begins. The published figure shows the plates starting about a quarter of the way along, and that is what section 11 measured - but a foil that starts late cannot reverse the drift at all, because the net work a conservative axial field does is q(phi_start - phi_end) and an ion that crosses the whole potential bump nets nothing. Set to zero so the foil spans the drift and the ion begins inside it. Handoff section 15.

foilReach.description: Distance from the analyser mid-plane to a mirror mouth, the scale the foil plate positions are expressed as fractions of.

foilOuter.description: Foil plate outer edge, measured from the mid-plane.

foilDriftSpan.description: Fraction of the drift the foil covers.

foilGrade.description: How far the foil bias is graded along the drift: 0 biases every slice at foilVolts, which is the PUBLISHED arrangement - the plate is at one voltage and the axial potential varies through its contoured SHAPE. Shipped at 0 as of 2026-09-02. A graded bias (1 ramps to zero at the far end) was an earlier mechanism of this model's own and is not what the instrument does; kept so the two can be compared.

convergence.description: How much the cap-to-cap gap narrows across the drift length. DERIVED from the spacer and its baseline, and reported because it is the quantity the earlier revisions of this template declared directly. 0.56 mm at the shipped values.

maxX.expression: midPlane - (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach
midPlane - (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach

minX.expression: midPlane + (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach
midPlane + (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach
